title: Character Over Achievement
author: Anthony Bradley
summary: Bradley argues that suburban obsession with college readiness produces impressive resumes but evil character in boys. High academic achievement without character formation creates impressive but morally broken men. Bradley challenges parents to prioritize character development over resume optimization. The piece argues that Christian households and schools often measure success by worldly metrics—grades, test scores, college admission—rather than godly character markers. Bradley contends that parenting should shape boys' souls first, achievement second, but most contemporary parenting inverts these priorities with predictable spiritual damage.
points: College readiness culture prioritizes impressive resume over moral character
High GPA can mask or accompany deep character defects and spiritual bankruptcy
Character formation requires deliberate prioritization; achievement culture crowds it out
Schools and churches often reward achievement while ignoring character breakdown
Boys need character-first parenting; resume success matters little without godly manhood
